newsitem.title: USA: Dozens hospitalized by mystery Texas gas leak.
newsitem.headline: Dozens hospitalized by mystery Texas gas leak.

text.p: Dozens of workers were rushed to hospitals on Tuesday after suffering severe breathing problems and nausea from a mystery gas leak at a Fort Worth office tower, officials said.

More than 200 people received emergency treatment at the scene and 72 were hospitalized. Ambulance crews carried workers out of the building on stretchers and rushed oxygen masks to many others who lay gasping on a grass bank, complaining of breathing troubles, nausea and dizziness.
Lt. Kent Worley of the Fort Worth Fire Department said hazardous materials experts had no idea what caused the health problems but that the worst of the danger was apparently over.

"They have not been able to find anything out of the ordinary so far. The meters they have, which look for a broad range of possibilities, haven't come up with anything," Worley said. "At this point it is still a mystery."
Office workers said the problems began on the sixth floor of the nine-story Overton Center office tower in southwest Fort Worth, and spread quickly.

"One lady had a seizure and we didn't know what was going on. People started vomiting, their eyes were burning and we were all getting lightheaded," said Mary Watson, one of the workers who was evacuated.
Worley said health officials had wanted to hospitalize 180 people but that many felt much better after taking oxygen, and opted not to go to hospital.
Seven area hospitals received the 72 office workers, but none of them was reported in serious condition and most were expected to return home later Tuesday.
Worley said most of those affected were customer service employees of United Parcel Service. About 1,100 people work in the office tower.
